sanskrit: atha pañcavaṭīṃ gacchann antarā raghunandanaḥ āsasāda mahākāyaṃ gṛdhraṃ bhīmaparākramam
english: Now, as the delight of Raghu's line was on his way to Pañcavaṭī, he encountered midway a vulture of enormous body and fearsome might.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā tau mahābhāgau vanasthaṃ rāmalakṣmaṇau menāte rākṣasaṃ pakṣiṃ bruvāṇau ko bhavān iti
english: Seeing that bird perched in the forest, the two illustrious ones, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, thought it a rākṣasa, and asked: "Who are you?"

sanskrit: sa tau madhurayā vācā saumyayā prīṇayann iva uvāca vatsa māṃ viddhi vayasyaṃ pitur ātmanaḥ
english: He, as if gladdening them with a sweet and gentle voice, said: "Know me, my child, as a companion of your own father."

sanskrit: sa taṃ pitṛsakhaṃ buddhvā pūjayām āsa rāghavaḥ sa tasya kulam avyagram atha papraccha nāma ca
english: Recognising him as his father's friend, Rāghava honoured him; then he calmly inquired about his lineage and name.

sanskrit: rāmasya vacanaṃ śrutvā kulam ātmānam eva ca ācacakṣe dvijas tasmai sarvabhūtasamudbhavam
english: Hearing Rāma's words, that twice-born one — for a bird too is twice-born — disclosed to him his lineage and his own origin, which traces back to the source of all living beings.

sanskrit: pūrvakāle mahābāho ye prajāpatayo 'bhavan tān me nigadataḥ sarvān āditaḥ śṛṇu rāghava
english: "O mighty-armed one, hear from the beginning as I recount all the Prajāpatis who existed in former times, O Rāghava."

sanskrit: kardamaḥ prathamas teṣāṃ vikṛtas tadanantaram śeṣaś ca saṃśrayaś caiva bahuputraś ca vīryavān
english: "Kardama is the first among them; Vikṛta comes next; then Śeṣa, Saṃśraya, and the valiant Bahuputra."

sanskrit: sthāṇur marīcir atriś ca kratuś caiva mahābalaḥ pulastyaś cāṅgirāś caiva pracetāḥ pulahas tathā
english: "Sthāṇu, Marīci, Atri, and the greatly powerful Kratu; Pulastya, Aṅgiras, Pracetas, and likewise Pulaha."

sanskrit: dakṣo vivasvān aparo 'riṣṭanemiś ca rāghava kaśyapaś ca mahātejās teṣām āsīc ca paścimaḥ
english: "Dakṣa, Vivasvān, and then Ariṣṭanemi, O Rāghava; and the greatly resplendent Kaśyapa was the last among them."

sanskrit: prajāpates tu dakṣasya babhūvur iti naḥ śrutam ṣaṣṭir duhitaro rāma yaśasvinyo mahāyaśaḥ
english: "The Prajāpati Dakṣa had sixty daughters — so we have heard — all renowned, O Rāma of great glory."

sanskrit: kaśyapaḥ pratijagrāha tāsām aṣṭau sumadhyamāḥ aditiṃ ca ditiṃ caiva danūm api ca kālakām
english: "Kaśyapa took eight of those slender-waisted women: Aditi and Diti, Danu, and also Kālakā,"

sanskrit: tāmrāṃ krodhavaśāṃ caiva manuṃ cāpy analām api tās tu kanyās tataḥ prītaḥ kaśyapaḥ punar abravīt
english: "Tāmrā, Krodhavaśa, Manu, and also Analā. Then Kaśyapa, well pleased, spoke again to those maidens:"

sanskrit: putrāṃs trailokyabhartṝn vai janayiṣyatha mat samān aditis tan manā rāma ditiś ca danur eva ca
english: "'You shall bear sons equal to me, lords of the three worlds.' Aditi agreed with that intent, O Rāma — as did Diti and Danu."

sanskrit: kālakā ca mahābāho śeṣās tv amanaso 'bhavan adityāṃ jajñire devās trayastriṃśad ariṃdama
english: "Kālakā too agreed, O mighty-armed one; the remaining ones were not of that mind. From Aditi were born the thirty-three gods, O subduer of foes."

sanskrit: ādityā vasavo rudrā aśvinau ca paraṃtapa ditis tv ajanayat putrān daityāṃs tāta yaśasvinaḥ
english: "The Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Aśvins, O scorcher of foes. Diti bore sons, the illustrious Daityas, my child."

sanskrit: teṣām iyaṃ vasumatī purāsīt savanārṇavā danus tv ajanayat putram aśvagrīvam ariṃdama
english: "This earth was formerly theirs alone, a sea of divine rites. Danu bore a son named Aśvagrīva, O subduer of foes."

sanskrit: narakaṃ kālakaṃ caiva kālakāpi vyajāyata krauñcīṃ bhāsīṃ tathā śyenīṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrīṃ tathā śukīm
english: "Naraka and Kālaka were born of Kālakā. And Tāmrā gave birth to five daughters: Krauñcī, Bhāsī, Śyenī, Dhṛtarāṣṭrī, and Śukī."

sanskrit: tāmrāpi suṣuve kanyāḥ pañcaitā lokaviśrutāḥ ulūkāñ janayat krauñcī bhāsī bhāsān vyajāyata
english: "These five daughters of Tāmrā are famed throughout the worlds. Krauñcī gave birth to owls; Bhāsī bore the bhāsa birds."

sanskrit: śyenī śyenāṃś ca gṛdhrāṃś ca vyajāyata sutejasaḥ dhṛtarāṣṭrī tu haṃsāṃś ca kalahaṃsāṃś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: "Śyenī bore hawks and vultures, all of great brilliance. Dhṛtarāṣṭrī bore all manner of geese and bar-headed geese,"

sanskrit: cakravākāṃś ca bhadraṃ te vijajñe sāpi bhāminī śukī natāṃ vijajñe tu natāyā vinatā sutā
english: "and cakravāka birds too did that fair lady produce. Śukī gave birth to Natā, and from Natā was born Vinatā."

sanskrit: daśakrodhavaśā rāma vijajñe 'py ātmasaṃbhavāḥ mṛgīṃ ca mṛgamandāṃ ca harīṃ bhadramadām api
english: "Krodhavaśa, O Rāma, bore ten daughters of her own: Mṛgī, Mṛgamandā, Hari, and Bhadramadā,"

sanskrit: mātaṅgīm atha śārdūlīṃ śvetāṃ ca surabhīṃ tathā sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpannāṃ surasāṃ kadrukām api
english: "Mātaṅgī, Śārdūlī, Śvetā, and Surabhī, and also Surasā endowed with all auspicious marks, and Kadrukā."

sanskrit: apatyaṃ tu mṛgāḥ sarve mṛgyā naravarottama ṛṣkāś ca mṛgamandāyāḥ sṛmarāś camarās tathā
english: "All deer are the offspring of Mṛgī, O best of men. From Mṛgamandā come bears, as well as sṛmaras and cāmaras."

sanskrit: tatas tv irāvatīṃ nāma jajñe bhadramadā sutām tasyās tv airāvataḥ putro lokanātho mahāgajaḥ
english: "Then Bhadramadā bore a daughter named Irāvatī; and Irāvatī's son is Airāvata, the great elephant who is lord of the worlds."

sanskrit: haryāś ca harayo 'patyaṃ vānarāś ca tapasvinaḥ golāṅgūlāṃś ca śārdūlī vyāghrāṃś cājanayat sutān
english: "From Hari come the haras and also the ascetic monkeys. Śārdūlī bore golāṅgūlas and tigers as her sons."

sanskrit: mātaṅgyās tv atha mātaṅgā apatyaṃ manujarṣabha diśāgajaṃ tu śvetākṣaṃ śvetā vyajanayat sutam
english: "From Mātaṅgī come elephants as her offspring, O bull among men. And Śvetā bore as her son the white-eyed directional elephant."

sanskrit: tato duhitarau rāma surabhir devy ajāyata rohiṇīṃ nāma bhadraṃ te gandharvīṃ ca yaśasvinīm
english: "Then, O Rāma, the goddess Surabhī bore two daughters — well be it with you — one named Rohiṇī, and the illustrious Gandharvī."

sanskrit: rohiṇy ajanayad gā vai gandharvī vājinaḥ sutān surasājanayan nāgān rāma kadrūś ca pannagān
english: "Rohiṇī bore cows; Gandharvī bore horses as her sons. Surasā bore the nāgas, O Rāma, and Kadrukā bore the serpents."

sanskrit: manur manuṣyāñ janayat kaśyapasya mahātmanaḥ brāhmaṇān kṣatriyān vaiśyāṃś śūdrāṃś ca manujarṣabha
english: "Manu bore humankind for the great-souled Kaśyapa — brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras, O bull among men."

sanskrit: mukhato brāhmaṇā jātā urasaḥ kṣatriyās tathā ūrubhyāṃ jajñire vaiśyāḥ padbhyāṃ śūdrā iti śrutiḥ
english: "Brāhmaṇas were born from his mouth; kṣatriyas likewise from his chest; vaiśyas were born from his thighs; śūdras from his feet — so the Vedic tradition declares."

sanskrit: sarvān puṇyaphalān vṛkṣān analāpi vyajāyata vinatā ca śukī pautrī kadrūś ca surasā svasā
english: "Analā also bore all trees bearing sacred fruits. Vinatā is the granddaughter of Śukī, and Kadrukā is the sister of Surasā."

sanskrit: kadrūr nāgasahaskraṃ tu vijajñe dharaṇīdharam dvau putrau vinatāyās tu garuḍo 'ruṇa eva ca
english: "Kadrukā bore a thousand nāgas who uphold the earth. Vinatā had two sons: Garuḍa and Aruṇa."

sanskrit: tasmāj jāto 'ham aruṇāt saṃpātiś ca mamāgrajaḥ jaṭāyur iti māṃ viddhi śyenīputram ariṃdama
english: "From that Aruṇa I was born, and Saṃpāti is my elder brother. Know me as Jaṭāyus, son of Śyenī, O subduer of foes."

sanskrit: so 'haṃ vāsasahāyas te bhaviṣyāmi yadīcchasi sītāṃ ca tāta rakṣiṣye tvayi yāte salakṣmaṇe
english: "I shall be a companion and protector for you, if you so wish. And I shall guard Sītā, my child, when you go out together with Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: jaṭāyuṣaṃ tu pratipūjya rāghavo mudā pariṣvajya ca saṃnato 'bhavat pitur hi śuśrāva sakhitvam ātmavāñ jaṭāyuṣā saṃkathitaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
english: Honouring Jaṭāyus, Rāghava embraced him joyfully and bowed in reverence; for that self-possessed one heard again and again from Jaṭāyus of the old friendship with his father.

sanskrit: sa tatra sītāṃ paridāya maithilīṃ sahaiva tenātibalena pakṣiṇā jagāma tāṃ pañcavaṭīṃ salakṣmaṇo ripūn didhakṣañ śalabhān ivānalaḥ
english: Entrusting Maithilī Sītā to that supremely powerful bird's care, he proceeded to that Pañcavaṭī together with Lakṣmaṇa, longing to burn his enemies as fire burns moths.

sanskrit: tataḥ pañcavaṭīṃ gatvā nānāvyālamṛgāyutām uvāca bhrātaraṃ rāmo lakṣmaṇaṃ dīptatejasaṃ
english: Then, having arrived at Pañcavaṭī — teeming with diverse serpents and wild beasts — Rāma addressed his brother, the blazing-splendoured Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: āgatāḥ sma yathoddiṣṭam amuṃ deśaṃ maharṣiṇā ayaṃ pañcavaṭī deśaḥ saumya puṣpitakānanaḥ
english: "We have arrived at this place as directed by the great sage. This, dear Lakṣmaṇa, is the region of Pañcavaṭī, with its flowering groves."

sanskrit: sarvataś cāryatāṃ dṛṣṭiḥ kānane nipuṇo hy asi āśramaḥ katarasmin no deśe bhavati saṃmataḥ
english: "Let your gaze range all around; you are skilled in forest matters. In which spot shall our hermitage suitably be made?"

sanskrit: ramate yatra vaidehī tvam ahaṃ caiva lakṣmaṇa tādṛśo dṛśyatāṃ deśaḥ saṃnikṛṣṭajalāśayaḥ
english: "Where Vaidehī may delight, and you and I as well, O Lakṣmaṇa — let such a place be found, one close to a body of water."

sanskrit: vanarāmaṇyakaṃ yatra jalarāmaṇyakaṃ tathā saṃnikṛṣṭaṃ ca yatra syāt samitpuṣpakuśodakam
english: "A place where the forest is charming and the water is charming, and where firewood, flowers, kuśa grass, and water are close at hand."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa lakmaṇaḥ saṃyatāñjaliḥ sītā samakṣaṃ kākutstham idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Thus addressed by Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa — hands folded in reverence — spoke these words to Kākutstha in the presence of Sītā:

sanskrit: paravān asmi kākutstha tvayi varṣaśataṃ sthite svayaṃ tu rucire deśe kriyatām iti māṃ vada
english: "I am subject to you, O Kākutstha — were you to stand thus a hundred years. Tell me yourself: 'Build it in this pleasing spot.'"

sanskrit: suprītas tena vākyena lakṣmaṇasya mahādyutiḥ vimṛśan rocayām āsa deśaṃ sarvaguṇānvitam
english: Greatly pleased by that speech of Lakṣmaṇa's, that one of great splendour, reflecting carefully, approved of a place endowed with every virtue.

sanskrit: sa taṃ ruciram ākramya deśam āśramakarmaṇi haste gṛhītvā hastena rāmaḥ saumitrim abravīt
english: Stepping onto that beautiful spot with the work of building the hermitage in mind, Rāma took the son of Sumitrā by the hand and said:

sanskrit: ayaṃ deśaḥ samaḥ śrīmān puṣpitair tarubhir vṛtaḥ ihāśramapadaṃ saumya yathāvat kartum arhasi
english: "This ground is level and beautiful, surrounded by flowering trees. Here, dear Lakṣmaṇa, you should build our hermitage properly."

sanskrit: iyam ādityasaṃkāśaiḥ padmaiḥ surabhigandhibhiḥ adūre dṛśyate ramyā padminī padmaśobhitā
english: "Not far away one can see this lovely lotus-pond, adorned with lotuses — fragrant lotuses that rival the sun — gleaming with lotus-blooms."

sanskrit: yathākhyātam agastyena muninā bhāvitātmanā iyaṃ godāvarī ramyā puṣpitais tarubhir vṛtā
english: "Just as described by the sage Agastya of purified soul, here flows the lovely Godāvarī, lined with flowering trees."

sanskrit: haṃsakāraṇḍavākīrṇā cakravākopaśobhitā nātidūre na cāsanne mṛgayūthanipīḍitā
english: "Thronged with geese and kāraṇḍava ducks, adorned with cakravāka birds, neither too far nor too close, frequented by herds of deer."

sanskrit: mayūranāditā ramyāḥ prāṃśavo bahukandarāḥ dṛśyante girayaḥ saumya phullais tarubhir āvṛtāḥ
english: "Resonant with the cries of peacocks, lovely and lofty, riddled with many caves, the hills are visible, dear Lakṣmaṇa, clad in full-blossomed trees."

sanskrit: sauvarṇe rājatais tāmrair deśe deśe ca dhātubhiḥ gavākṣitā ivābhānti gajāḥ paramabhaktibhiḥ
english: "With golden, silver, and copper minerals here and there across the slopes, the mountains gleam like elephants adorned with the most devout markings."

sanskrit: sālais tālais tamālaiś ca kharjūraiḥ panasāmrakaiḥ nīvārais timiśaiś caiva puṃnāgaiś copaśobhitāḥ
english: "Adorned with śāla trees, palmyras, tamāla, date-palms, jackfruit and mango trees, nīvāra grass, timiśa trees, and puṃnāga trees,"

sanskrit: cūtair aśokais tilakaiś campakaiḥ ketakair api puṣpagulmalatopetais tais tais tarubhir āvṛtāḥ
english: "and covered with mango, aśoka, tilaka, campaka, and ketaka trees, as well as with flowering shrubs and creepers of every kind."

sanskrit: candanaiḥ syandanair nīpaiḥ panasair lakucair api dhavāśvakarṇakhadiraiḥ śamīkiṃśukapāṭalaiḥ
english: "With sandalwood, syandana, nīpa, jackfruit, and lakuca trees; dhava, aśvakarṇa, khadira, śamī, kiṃśuka, and pāṭala trees."

sanskrit: idaṃ puṇyam idaṃ medhyam idaṃ bahumṛgadvijam iha vatsyāma saumitre sārdham etena pakṣiṇā
english: "This place is sacred, this place is pure, this place abounds in animals and birds. Here we shall dwell, O son of Sumitrā, together with this bird."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā acireṇāśramaṃ bhrātuś cakāra sumahābalaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa — slayer of enemy heroes and supremely mighty — in no time built his brother's hermitage.

sanskrit: parṇaśālāṃ suvipulāṃ tatra saṃghātamṛttikām sustambhāṃ maskaraiḥ dīrghaiḥ kṛtavaṃśāṃ suśobhanām
english: A leaf-hut, spacious and well-plastered with earth, firmly pillared, framed with long bamboo poles, and very beautiful.

sanskrit: sa gatvā lakṣmaṇaḥ śrīmān nadīṃ godāvarīṃ tadā snātvā padmāni cādāya saphalaḥ punar āgataḥ
english: The glorious Lakṣmaṇa then went to the river Godāvarī; having bathed and gathered lotuses, he returned having accomplished his errand.

sanskrit: tataḥ puṣpabaliṃ kṛtvā śāntiṃ ca sa yathāvidhi darśayām āsa rāmāya tad āśramapadaṃ kṛtam
english: Then, having offered a floral oblation and performed the pacificatory rites in the prescribed manner, he presented to Rāma the hermitage thus completed.

sanskrit: sa taṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛtaṃ saumyam āśramaṃ saha sītayā rāghavaḥ parṇaśālāyāṃ harṣam āhārayat param
english: Seeing that hermitage built — gentle and fair — together with Sītā, Rāghava entered the leaf-hut and felt the utmost joy.

sanskrit: susaṃhṛṣṭaḥ pariṣvajya bāhubhyāṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ tadā atisnigdhaṃ ca gāḍhaṃ ca vacanaṃ cedam abravīt
english: Greatly delighted, he then embraced Lakṣmaṇa with both arms, and spoke these words, tender and heartfelt:

sanskrit: prīto 'smi te mahat karma tvayā kṛtam idaṃ prabho pradeyo yannimittaṃ te pariṣvaṅgo mayā kṛtaḥ
english: "I am pleased with you, O lord; great is the deed you have done. For this reason the embrace I have given you is your due reward."

sanskrit: bhāvajñena kṛtajñena dharmajñena ca lakṣmaṇa tvayā putreṇa dharmātmā na saṃvṛttaḥ pitā mama
english: "With you as a son — one who knows feelings, one who is grateful, one who knows dharma, O Lakṣmaṇa — my father, that righteous soul, has not truly passed away."

sanskrit: evaṃ lakṣmaṇam uktvā tu rāghavo lakṣmivardhanaḥ tasmin deśe bahuphale nyavasat sa sukhaṃ vaśī
english: Having spoken thus to Lakṣmaṇa, Rāghava — that increaser of glory, self-controlled — dwelt happily in that fruit-abundant place.

sanskrit: kaṃ cit kālaṃ sa dharmātmā sītayā lakṣmaṇena ca anvāsyamāno nyavasat svargaloke yathāmaraḥ
english: For some time that righteous soul dwelt there, attended by Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa, like an immortal in the world of heaven.

sanskrit: vasatas tasya tu sukhaṃ rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ śaradvyapāye hemanta ṛtur iṣṭaḥ pravartate
english: As the great-souled Rāghava was dwelling there in contentment, with autumn's passing, the beloved season of hemanta — early winter — commenced.

sanskrit: sa kadā cit prabhātāyāṃ śarvaryāṃ raghunandanaḥ prayayāv abhiṣekārthaṃ ramyāṃ godāvarīṃ nadīm
english: One day, as night turned to dawn, the delight of Raghu's line set out to bathe at the lovely river Godāvarī.

sanskrit: prahvaḥ kalaśahastas taṃ sītayā saha vīryavān pṛṣṭhato 'nuvrajan bhrātā saumitrir idam abravīt
english: The valiant son of Sumitrā, bowing respectfully, water-pot in hand, followed behind him along with Sītā, and spoke these words:

sanskrit: ayaṃ sa kālaḥ saṃprāptaḥ priyo yas te priyaṃvada alaṃkṛta ivābhāti yena saṃvatsaraḥ śubhaḥ
english: "That beloved season you hold dear has arrived, O sweet-spoken one — by which the auspicious year seems adorned, as if decked out in finery."

sanskrit: nīhāraparuṣo lokaḥ pṛthivī sasyamālinī jalāny anupabhogyāni subhago havyavāhanaḥ
english: "The world grows rough with frost; the earth is garlanded with grain; the waters are no longer agreeable to touch; fire, the carrier of oblations, is most welcome."

sanskrit: navāgrayaṇapūjābhir abhyarcya pitṛdevatāḥ kṛtāgrayaṇakāḥ kāle santo vigatakalmaṣāḥ
english: "The virtuous, having worshipped the ancestors and the gods with offerings of the new first-fruits, complete the new-grain rite in due season, purged of all impurity."

sanskrit: prājyakāmā janapadāḥ saṃpannataragorasāḥ vicaranti mahīpālā yātrārthaṃ vijigīṣavaḥ
english: "The kingdoms, rich in desire for plenty and blessed with abundant dairy produce; the earth's protectors rove about, eager for conquest, setting out on campaign."

sanskrit: sevamāne dṛḍhaṃ sūrye diśam antakasevitām vihīnatilakeva strī nottarā dik prakāśate
english: "As the sun clings steadfastly to the direction frequented by Yama, the northern quarter shines no more brightly, like a woman deprived of her tilaka."

sanskrit: prakṛtyā himakośāḍhyo dūrasūryaś ca sāmpratam yathārthanāmā suvyaktaṃ himavān himavān giriḥ
english: "Rich in frost by nature and now with the sun far away, the mountain Himavat lives up to its name — the snow-mountain — most manifestly."

sanskrit: atyantasukhasaṃcārā madhyāhne sparśataḥ sukhāḥ divasāḥ subhagādityāś chāyāsaliladurbhagāḥ
english: "The days bring extreme ease for travel; at noon they are pleasant to the touch; the sun in them is pleasant — yet shade and water are unwelcome."

sanskrit: mṛdusūryāḥ sanīhārāḥ paṭuśītāḥ samārutāḥ śūnyāraṇyā himadhvastā divasā bhānti sāmpratam
english: "The days now shine with a mild sun, veiled in mist, sharply cold, with steady breezes, the forests bare of creatures, blasted by frost."

sanskrit: nivṛttākāśaśayanāḥ puṣyanītā himāruṇāḥ śītā vṛddhatarāyāmās triyāmā yānti sāmpratam
english: "The nights now pass — their open-sky sleeping done, led onward by the Puṣya star, reddened by frost, cold, and grown longer still."

sanskrit: ravisaṃkrāntasaubhāgyas tuṣārāruṇamaṇḍalaḥ niḥśvāsāndha ivādarśaś candramā na prakāśate
english: "His beauty transferred to the sun, the moon's orb reddened by frost — like a mirror clouded by breath — the moon no longer shines."

sanskrit: jyotsnā tuṣāramalinā paurṇamāsyāṃ na rājate sīteva cātapaśyāmā lakṣyate na tu śobhate
english: "The moonlight, soiled by frost, does not gleam even on a full-moon night; it appears, like Sītā darkened by the sun's glare, but does not shine with beauty."

sanskrit: prakṛtyā śītalasparśo himaviddhaś ca sāmpratam pravāti paścimo vāyuḥ kāle dviguṇaśītalaḥ
english: "Cold to the touch by nature, and now pierced by frost, the western wind blows in this season twice as cold as before."

sanskrit: bāṣpacchannāny araṇyāni yavagodhūmavanti ca śobhante 'bhyudite sūrye nadadbhiḥ krauñcasārasaiḥ
english: "The forests, wrapped in mist, filled with barley and wheat, grow beautiful at sunrise, resounding with the cries of krauñca birds and sārasa cranes."

sanskrit: kharjūrapuṣpākṛtibhiḥ śirobhiḥ pūrṇataṇḍulaiḥ śobhante kiṃ cidālambāḥ śālayaḥ kanakaprabhāḥ
english: "Rice plants, golden in lustre, slightly drooping with heads full of grain shaped like date-palm blossoms, stand beautifully."

sanskrit: mayūkhair upasarpadbhir himanīhārasaṃvṛtaiḥ dūram abhyuditaḥ sūryaḥ śaśāṅka iva lakṣyate
english: "With its rays drawing near yet veiled in frost and mist, the sun rising at a great distance appears like the moon."

sanskrit: agrāhyavīryaḥ pūrvāhṇe madhyāhne sparśataḥ sukhaḥ saṃraktaḥ kiṃ cid āpāṇḍur ātapaḥ śobhate kṣitau
english: "Lacking strength to warm in the morning, pleasant to the touch at noon, deep red and yet faintly pale, the sunlight shines beautifully upon the earth."

sanskrit: avaśyāyanipātena kiṃ cit praklinnaśādvalā vanānāṃ śobhate bhūmir niviṣṭataruṇātapā
english: "Wet with the fall of dew, the grassy ground of the forests, bathed in the young morning sunlight, shines beautifully."

sanskrit: avaśyāyatamonaddhā nīhāratamasāvṛtāḥ prasuptā iva lakṣyante vipuṣpā vanarājayaḥ
english: "Swathed in the darkness of dew, covered over by the darkness of mist, the rows of trees in the forest — flowerless — appear as though deep in slumber."

sanskrit: bāṣpasaṃchannasalilā rutavijñeyasārasāḥ himārdravālukais tīraiḥ sarito bhānti sāmpratam
english: "Their waters covered with vapour, their sārasa cranes identifiable only by their cries, with banks of frost-wet sand — the rivers shine now in this season."

sanskrit: tuṣārapatanāc caiva mṛdutvād bhāskarasya ca śaityād agāgrastham api prāyeṇa rasavaj jalam
english: "From the fall of frost, from the mildness of the sun, and from the cold — even water not seized by fire is, for the most part, still savoured warm."

sanskrit: jarājarjaritaiḥ parṇaiḥ śīrṇakesarakarṇikaiḥ nālaśeṣā himadhvastā na bhānti kamalākarāḥ
english: "Their leaves yellowed and withered with age, their stamens and pericarp shed, reduced to mere stalks, blasted by frost — the lotus pools no longer shine."

sanskrit: asmiṃs tu puruṣavyāghra kāle duḥkhasamanvitaḥ tapaś carati dharmātmā tvadbhaktyā bharataḥ pure
english: "In this very season, O tiger among men, Bharata, that righteous soul, is practising austerity in the city, afflicted with sorrow, out of devotion to you."

sanskrit: tyaktvā rājyaṃ ca mānaṃ ca bhogāṃś ca vividhān bahūn tapasvī niyatāhāraḥ śete śīte mahītale
english: "Having renounced the kingdom, honour, and many varied pleasures, he sleeps — a man of austerity with regulated diet — on the cold bare ground."

sanskrit: so 'pi velām imāṃ nūnam abhiṣekārtham udyataḥ vṛtaḥ prakṛtibhir nityaṃ prayāti sarayūṃ nadīm
english: "He too, at this very hour, no doubt rising for his ablutions, ever attended by the counsellors of the realm, proceeds to the river Sarayū."

sanskrit: atyantasukhasaṃvṛddhaḥ sukumāro himārditaḥ kathaṃ tv apararātreṣu sarayūm avagāhate
english: "Raised in the utmost comfort, tender by nature, now tormented by the frost — how does he plunge into the Sarayū in the hours before dawn?"

sanskrit: padmapatrekṣaṇaḥ śyāmaḥ śrīmān nirudaro mahān dharmajñaḥ satyavādī ca hrīniṣedho jitendriyaḥ
english: "Lotus-petal-eyed, dark-complexioned, glorious, with a slender waist yet great in stature, knowing dharma, truthful, restrained by modesty, master of his senses —"

sanskrit: priyābhibhāṣī madhuro dīrghabāhur ariṃdamaḥ saṃtyajya vividhān saukhyān āryaṃ sarvātmanāśritaḥ
english: "— sweet of speech, gentle, long-armed, subduer of foes — having given up various pleasures entirely, he has taken refuge wholly in the noble path."

sanskrit: jitaḥ svargas tava bhrātrā bharatena mahātmanā vanastham api tāpasye yas tvām anuvidhīyate
english: "Heaven has been conquered by your brother Bharata, that great-souled one, who, even though you are in the forest, follows your example in austerity."

sanskrit: na pitryam anuvarntante mātṛkaṃ dvipadā iti khyāto lokapravādo 'yaṃ bharatenānyathākṛtaḥ
english: "'Bipeds follow the father's nature, not the mother's' — so runs the world-famous saying; but Bharata has made it otherwise."

sanskrit: bhartā daśaratho yasyāḥ sādhuś ca bharataḥ sutaḥ kathaṃ nu sāmbā kaikeyī tādṛśī krūradarśinī
english: "She whose husband is Daśaratha and whose son is the virtuous Bharata — how, then, is that Kaikeyī, our own mother, so cruel in her designs?"

sanskrit: ity evaṃ lakṣmaṇe vākyaṃ snehād bruvati dhārmike parivādaṃ jananyās tam asahan rāghavo 'bravīt
english: As the righteous Lakṣmaṇa spoke these words out of affection, Rāghava — unable to bear that reproach of his mother — replied:

sanskrit: na te 'mbā madhyamā tāta garhitavyā kathaṃ cana tām evekṣvākunāthasya bharatasya kathāṃ kuru
english: "Your middle mother must not be reviled in any way, my child. Speak rather only of Bharata, the lord of the Ikṣvāku line."

sanskrit: niścitāpi hi me buddhir vanavāse dṛḍhavratā bharatasnehasaṃtaptā bāliśīkriyate punaḥ
english: "Even my mind — firm in its resolve to dwell in the forest, steadfast in its vow — is again made foolish, scorched as it is by longing for Bharata."

sanskrit: ity evaṃ vilapaṃs tatra prāpya godāvarīṃ nadīm cakre 'bhiṣekaṃ kākutsthaḥ sānujaḥ saha sītayā
english: Lamenting thus, Kākutstha reached the river Godāvarī there, and together with his younger brother and with Sītā performed his ablutions.

sanskrit: tarpayitvātha salilais te pitṝn daivatāni ca stuvanti smoditaṃ sūryaṃ devatāś ca samāhitāḥ
english: Then, having offered water to the ancestors and the divinities, they praised the sun newly risen and the gods, composed and intent.

sanskrit: kṛtābhiṣekaḥ sa rarāja rāmaḥ sītādvitīyaḥ saha lakṣmaṇena kṛtābhiṣekas tv agarājaputryā rudraḥ sanandir bhagavān iveśaḥ
english: Having completed his ablutions, Rāma shone resplendent — with Sītā as his second and together with Lakṣmaṇa — as the blessed lord Rudra, ever joyful, shines with the daughter of the mountain king after his own ablutions.
